2609.29802.title: Learning to Ideate for Scientific Impact
2609.29802.paper_summary: Scientific ideation is increasingly mediated by large language models, but current ideation systems are usually trained and evaluated on immediately judgeable proxies such as novelty, clarity, and feasibility. This leaves open whether delayed signals of scientific uptake can be used as feedback for steering models toward research directions with higher expected \emph{impact}. We study this question using citation-normalized impact as a noisy but scalable proxy for scholarly uptake. We construct a large-scale dataset from over 100K computer science papers by extracting goal-conditioned idea descriptions and assigning each paper an ordinal, year-normalized citation label. We then train a goal-conditioned reward model to predict citation-impact labels from research goal and idea pairs, and use this reward to align an idea generator through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. To reduce circularity, we evaluate generated ideas with a held-out, reference-grounded protocol that compares model outputs against historical ideas under the same research goal and weights judgments by the reference idea's citation-impact label. Experiments show that our RL-tuned model consistently produces ideas with higher estimated impact than both the base model and supervised fine-tuning baselines. Our findings position scientific impact as a practical, outcome-grounded feedback signal for aligning LLMs in open-ended scientific discovery.
2609.29802.paper_summary_zh: 科學創意越來越多地受到大型語言模型的調節，但當前的創意系統通常是在可立即評判的代理指標上進行訓練和評估，例如新穎性、清晰度和可行性。這使得尚不清楚延遲的科學採納信號是否可以用作反饋，以引導模型朝向具有更高預期\emph{影響}的研究方向。我們使用引用標準化的影響作為學術採納的嘈雜但可擴展的代理來研究這個問題。我們從超過10萬篇計算機科學論文中構建了一個大規模數據集，提取目標條件的想法描述，並為每篇論文分配一個有序的、年標準化的引用標籤。然後，我們訓練一個目標條件的獎勵模型，從研究目標和想法對中預測引用影響標籤，並使用這個獎勵通過監督微調和隨後的強化學習來對齊想法生成器。為了減少循環性，我們使用一個保留的、參考為基礎的協議來評估生成的想法，該協議將模型輸出與相同研究目標下的歷史想法進行比較，並根據參考想法的引用影響標籤對判斷進行加權。實驗表明，我們的強化學習調整模型持續產生的想法具有比基礎模型和監督微調基準更高的預估影響。我們的發現將科學影響定位為一種實用的、以結果為基礎的反饋信號，用於在開放式科學發現中對齊大型語言模型。
